Roberto 'Pico' Lopes qualifies to play for Cape Verde through his father(Image: ©INPHO/James Lawlor)

Shamrock Rovers defender Roberto “Pico” Lopes is living out his World Cup dream with Cape Verde – and his biggest fans are following him across America in a giant camper van!

The Dubliner’s wife Leah, their eight-month-old baby and four other family members are braving a 30-foot RV to cheer him on.

The rolling family party will be hard to miss as it cruises down the US highways, decked out with a massive flag featuring Pico’s face. Ireland missed out on what would have been our fourth World Cup appearance so many of the Boys in Green faithful are adopting Lopes’s Cape Verde for the showpiece event in North America, which started on Thursday night.

"Verde" even translates from Portuguese as "green" – so the links are obvious as Irish supporters weigh up who to shout for this summer.

Pico Lopes has 44 caps for Cape Verde(Image: Getty Images)

Speaking on RTE’s Liveline, Leah couldn’t contain her excitement about the ultimate family road trip.

“Six adults and an eight-month-old in nappies,” laughed Leah. “I don’t know what we’re doing, but we’ll have great craic and we’ll have great memories and we’ll probably end up killing each other by the end of it, but we’ll see how it goes!”

Irish-born Pico, who qualifies to play for the African nation through his dad, and his family will start in an Atlanta Airbnb before Leah’s father, Martin, takes the wheel of the massive camper van, driving them all the way down to Miami and across to Texas.

Shamrock Rovers captain Roberto 'Pico' Lopes lifted the FAI Cup in 2025(Image: INPHO/Ryan Byrne)

“He just gives everything to football,” Leah said proudly. “I said to him, you know, imagine little baby Pico, like, imagine telling him, you’re going to play in a World Cup one day...

“To see him walk out on that pitch, I’ll just be so, so happy for him.”

His mother Judy is just as thrilled, saying the whole family at home is “buzzing” as they count down.

“We’ve been waiting so long for kickoff and it’s almost here,” Judy beamed. “He’s committed. He’s hardworking, works hard at everything he does... He’s the whole package.”

Shamrock Rovers’ Pico Lopes was born in Ireland(Image: ©INPHO/Ryan Byrne)

Meanwhile, Priory Market in Tallaght - where Shamrock Rovers play - are holding a special World Cup watching party for Cape Verde’s opener against Spain on Monday.

“Pico has been a huge supporter of Priory Market from the very beginning – even before we opened our doors,” they said.

“He was the one who turned on the lights at our very first Christmas celebration and has remained a familiar face and great friend of the market ever since.

“Bring your friends, soak up the atmosphere, and help us send all of Tallaght’s support his way. We’re so grateful for everything Pico has done for our community.”
